description: ROC-AUC of the official chemprop v2 message-passing backbone on the Paper-A probe cohort — the same cohort as the Morgan-FP + XGBoost probe in metrics/by_metric/metal_activity_transfer.json.  --mode cross gives the leave-one-metal-out column (the paper's Table-1 cross), --mode within gives the stratified 5-fold CV inside each metal (Table-1 within).  Answers BLK-PA3: is the cross-metal collapse an artefact of a weak backbone?
model: chemprop v2 AtomMessagePassing (d_h=300, depth=3) + BinaryClassificationFFN (single pooled head, no metal features)
data_source: MetalCytoToxDB (Krasnov et al., J. Med. Chem. 2026, 69(8), 8838) — probe cohort
cohort_rule: per metal: MetalCytotoxDataset.from_csv(CytotoxFilter(time_threshold=24.0, ic50_min=0.01, metal_whitelist=[m])) then collapse_duplicates (one row per unique ligand, label = majority, ties -> ACTIVE)
leakage_rule: a ligand appearing in the held-out metal's test set is dropped from the LOMO training pool
honest_framing_note: PA3 chemprop v2 (AtomMessagePassing d_h=300, depth=3) + single pooled BinaryClassificationFFN (1x300, dropout=0.0) on the Paper-A probe cohort (MetalCytotoxDataset + CytotoxFilter(time<=24.0h, ic50>=0.01uM) + collapse_duplicates, leak-dropped train pool). mode=both; 25 cross (fold, seed) runs in 2.57 min wall.  AUCs are MEASURED with sklearn roc_auc_score on the sigmoid of the pooled head's logit.  Same cohort as metrics/by_metric/metal_activity_transfer.json (the XGB probe); the comparison isolates the scorer, not the cohort.
why: BLK-PA3: the paper's Claim-1 collapse is measured with a Morgan-FP + XGBoost probe, and the 'it is the metal axis, not a broken backbone' argument rested on MoleculeNet (where this repo's D-MPNN loses to the chemprop reference on 4/4 tasks).  This run replaces the scorer with the official chemprop v2 message-passing backbone on the SAME cohort and the SAME splits, so the comparison isolates the scorer.

cross_only_first_run.note: The first PA3 launch ran --mode cross only.  The rerun (mode=both) reproduced the cross column within GPU bf16 run-to-run variation: e.g. Ru seed42 0.5697 -> 0.5467, Re seed42 0.7583 -> 0.7607.  The 5-seed metal means moved by <=0.02.  Non-determinism is from cuDNN/bf16 reductions; the script seeds torch and numpy but does not call torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True).

verdict_vs_BLK_PA3: CHEMPROP REPRODUCES THE CROSS-METAL COLLAPSE ON 2 OF 5 METALS (Ir, Rh), with a within-minus-cross penalty that is positive on 4 OF 5 (Ru, Ir, Rh, Re) — the same sign as the XGB probe.  It is significantly ABOVE chance only on Ru, Re and significantly BELOW chance on Ir; Rh, Os sit in the null band.  Ru: cross 0.5621 (XGB 0.6179, -0.0558); within 0.7853 (XGB 0.8271); penalty +0.2232. Ir: cross 0.4841 (XGB 0.5276, -0.0435); within 0.7901 (XGB 0.8430); penalty +0.3060. Rh: cross 0.4915 (XGB 0.5190, -0.0275); within 0.6658 (XGB 0.6974); penalty +0.1743. Os: cross 0.5559 (XGB 0.4950, +0.0609); within 0.4133 (XGB 0.4960); penalty -0.1425. Re: cross 0.7368 (XGB 0.4429, +0.2939); within 0.8972 (XGB 0.9480); penalty +0.1604.
caveats: Per-metal test folds are small for Rh (n=51), Os (n=36) and Re (n=74).  The label-permutation null on the fixed seed-42 ranking is the reference used here (1,000 shuffles, matching metal_activity_transfer_permutation_null.json); at those sizes the null sd is ~0.09-0.11, so a nominal 0.5 is not the right line.

Only the CROSS column is seed-42 for the permutation null and the bootstrap CI; the reported cross AUCs are 5-seed means.  The CI's observed_auc is the seed-42 ranking, so it sits inside the seed spread around the 5-seed mean.
GPU bf16 training is not bit-reproducible run-to-run (~0.01-0.03 per-seed AUC drift).  Metal means are stable to <=0.02 across two independent launches.

The scorer is a single pooled BinaryClassificationFFN over the chemprop encoder with no metal features — deliberately matching the XGB probe's contract.  The existing per-metal-head chemprop LOMO (metal_lomo_chemprop_v2.json) is a different, non-comparable design.
